title: Acceptance Standard for Insurance Binders: Binder Acceptance Days on Wayfare Driver Agreements
content:
This acceptance standard of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product defines how many days an insurance binder is accepted for.

## 1. Definitions

1.1 **Binder acceptance days.** The calendar days, counted from the day support records it, for which an insurance binder uploaded to the standing record is accepted as the auto insurance on file.

1.2 **The binder.** The latest auto insurance upload on the standing record. Its **upload date** and **printed end date** are the date and the expiry date shown on that upload entry.

1.3 **Recording day.** The day support records the binder.

## 2. Standard

2.1 A binder updates the agreement only when support records it: the auto insurance expiry date on the agreement becomes the recording day plus the binder acceptance days, whatever end date is printed on the binder.

2.2 The binder acceptance days are 45 days.

2.3 The binder acceptance days never run past the binder's printed end date. This limit is applied last, to the binder acceptance days as counted before it, that count being taken as zero if it is below zero: the binder acceptance days are the lower of that count and the days from the recording day to the printed end date. The limit can only lower the count; it never raises it.

2.4 No rounding applies; the binder acceptance days are a whole number of days.

## 3. Worked examples (hypothetical binders, recording day 2026-07-01)

| Upload date | Printed end date | Days from recording day to printed end date | Binder acceptance days | Auto insurance expiry date on the agreement after recording |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-28 | 2026-09-30 | 91 | 45 | 2026-08-15 |
| 2026-06-28 | 2026-07-31 | 30 | 30 | 2026-07-31 |

In the first row the lower of 45 and 91 is 45, so the 45 days stand and the agreement shows 2026-08-15 although the binder prints 2026-09-30. In the second row the lower of 45 and 30 is 30, so the acceptance days stop at 30.
